We welcome you to the Youth Commission meeting.

If you wish to address the Commission during the meeting, please complete a speaker’s card and
give it to the secretary. The maximum time for addressing the Commission is five minutes. If
you wish to address the Commission on an item which appears on the agenda, your comments will
be heard during the Commission’s discussion of that item. If you wish to address the Commission
on a subject which does not appear on the agenda but related to recreation or community service,
you may make your presentation under agenda item VII. Please be advised that the Commission
cannot, under the State of California’s Ralph M. Brown Act, take action on any item which does
not appear on the agenda.

When making your presentation, please give your name and address for the record. Please make
your statement as brief as possible. Thank you.

I.  Roll Call

II.  Flag Salute

III.  Approval of the Minutes of the regular meeting of April 12, 2022

Minutes
  Alhambra Youth
  Commission May 10, 2022

The Alhambra Youth Commission was called to order at 6:15 PM on May 10, 2022 at Almansor Park,
800 S. Almansor Street, Alhambra, CA.

Commission Members Present: D. Andrade, B. Gonzalez, T. Hernandez, M. Webster, N. Quach
Commission Members Absent: J. Cooper, A. Gutierrez, M. Munson, Z.Oliva, L. Tran, J. Quach

Also present: Deputy Director - Brie Houghton

Flag Salute

Approval of Minutes
President N. Quach moved to approve the Minutes of April 12, 2022. Adjourned Regular Meeting.
Motioned by Commissioner D. Andrade and Seconded by T. Hernandez.

Staff Report
Deputy Director B. Houghton mentioned at the last City Council meeting it was voted to resume
meetings back to Zoom. Starting next month, all Council meetings will be held via Zoom until
further notice. Deputy Director B. Houghton then thanked N. Quach, for attending and
participating in all Tech Talks. The Deputy Director acknowledged the seniors loved him, and the
help from the Tech Talks. She had suggested that other Commissioners should attend Tech Talks
and that the commission should be working together as a team. She reminded them the Tech
Talks are held on the first Thursday of every month, starting at 4:00 pm. The Deputy Director said
she hopes to get more seniors to attend once the lunch program resumes in-person meals.
Commissioners were advised if they have travel plans for the summer and we need to take a break
to inform City staff by email so they can make other arrangements if needed.
Discussion of the Youth Summit
President N. Quach mentioned the Youth Summit was postponed until Fall 2022. Deputy Director
B. Houghton opened the topic of the Youth Summit with a few notes on why the event was
pushed back. Events should be planned accordingly, with 6 to 8 months in preparation. She stated
the Commissioners needed to work together as a team to meet the quota for the work that was
being delegated to them. She also said the assignments could be reassigned if need be. She
emphasized their school schedules but suggested having better communication so progress could
be made on the event. She said City staff were there to help, not to take over, just to assist. She
asked the Commissioners to provide updates and respond to emails. Deputy Director B.
Houghton talked about the youth of the year, providing suggestions on how the youth would be
judged on a year's worth of volunteering and the voting then would be in the Spring before the
school year is over. She asked for the Commissioners to do more research, on other Youth
Summits, and provide a timeline for the next meeting. President N. Quach shared with the
Commission his meeting with the Chamber of Commerce, and how they agreed to provide lunch
for the Summit. They discussed the vision and format of how the Youth Summit would be less of a
Gallery walk and more informational. He went on to state the importance of advocacy and
activism on how City Officials would be invited to start a dialogue on what needs to be done
within the City. They could have youth town halls, and youth workshops and invite other young
people to attend.
 Deputy Director asked President N. Quach what age group is envisioned, as the target
audience when he mentions the Youth Summit. President N. Quach mentions a broad
spectrum of ages. Director B. Houghton proposes how they can use different avenues to
accommodate the different age groups. Commissioner Webster stated how she felt the
Commission is going back and forth on the Summit theme because last it was education and
now they're back to discussing advocacy. Director B. Houghton suggests they tailor the theme
or title of the Summit to a specific subject. She asked the commissioners to research other
Youth Summits and come to the next meeting to present their ideas and or findings.
Commissioner Gonzalez shared she has survey results and how she could not upload them to
the Matrix. She was asked by Director B. Houghton to keep the data for reference for the
planning of the upcoming Youth Summit. It was asked of the Commissioner to resend the
Matrix link to the Commission and City staff so information could be uploaded.
Oral Communications
No orals at this time.
Commission Orals
Commissioner B. Gonzales gave her resignation from the Youth Commission on May 10,
2022, her reason being she's in her last year of High School and wants to focus on college. She
thanked the Commission and President N. Quach for bringing in new members. Director B.
Houghton asked her to send an email with her official resignation so she could forward it to
the City Clerk. President N. Quach said to was sad to see her leave. President N. Quach
followed up on an inquiry about the possibility and or progress of a Youth Commission
Instagram. Director B. Houghton stated the standard is no other City Commission has its own
account, and that there are laws on what can and can not be done because of the Brown Act
and ADA Social Media laws. She goes on to state the City prefers to keep it to the City
account. Before they could even push that further to get it approved content needs to be
structured perhaps in the future after the first Youth Summit and other events she'll revisit it
with upper management but as of right now it's limited content and it's preferred to stick to
the City account.
Adjournment
President N. Quach motioned for adjournment at approximately 7:06 pm. It was motioned by
Commission Webster and seconded by Commissioner Andrade.
